era: The One Who Fulfilled His Pledge
teaser: An arrow meant for the Prophet's ﷺ face went into Talhah's hand instead. He carried the mark for life.
quran_mention: «فَمِنْهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ» — 'among them is he who has fulfilled his vow' (33:23). The Prophet ﷺ used that same expression of Talhah.

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: A merchant of Quraysh who hated sitting still
layers.content:
He was Talhah ibn Ubaydullah ibn Uthman ibn Amr ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd ibn Taym ibn Murra — Banu Taym of Quraysh, the same clan as Abu Bakr. His kunya was Abu Muhammad, after his son. His mother was as-Sa'ba bint Abdullah al-Hadrami.

Those who described him said he was a dark man with a great deal of hair, neither tightly curled nor straight, with a handsome face and a narrow nose. When he walked, he walked fast. He did not dye his hair. Later in life he liked saffron-dyed clothes, and Umar once took him aside about wearing dyed cloth in ihram: you men are imams, he said, and people copy what they see.

His trade took him north to the markets of Syria. Quraysh counted him among their forbearing men, the ones who did not lose their temper in a quarrel. One saying of his tells you the shape of him: 'The least fault for a man is to sit in his house.' Idleness was the smallest charge anyone could bring against him, and the one he refused to earn.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: A monk in Busra asked him one question
layers.content:
He was standing in the market of Busra when a monk called down from his hermitage: is anyone at this festival from the people of the Haram? Talhah said, 'Yes, I am.'

The monk asked, 'Has Ahmad appeared yet?' Talhah asked who Ahmad was. The son of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, said the monk — the last of the Prophets, who will come out of the Haram and emigrate to a land of palm trees and lava beds. Then: 'Beware lest you be outstripped.'

The words lodged in his chest. He rode hard for Makkah and asked for news. There was news: Muhammad the trustworthy had said he was a Prophet, and Abu Bakr had followed him. Talhah went straight to Abu Bakr. 'Have you followed this man?' 'Yes,' said Abu Bakr. 'Go to him, and follow him. He is calling to the truth.'

Abu Bakr walked him to the Prophet ﷺ. Talhah became Muslim and repeated the monk's words, and the Prophet ﷺ was glad.

The bill came at once. Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, whom Quraysh called their Lion, bound Abu Bakr and Talhah together with one rope, and Banu Taym did not lift a hand for them. That is why the two were called the comrades.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The scout who missed Badr and was counted anyway
layers.content:
When the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah, Talhah was on the road home from Syria with a caravan. They met near al-Kharrar. Talhah dressed the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr in Syrian garments and told them the Muslims of Madinah thought them slow in coming, so the Prophet ﷺ quickened his pace. Talhah turned back to Makkah, settled his affairs, and then brought Abu Bakr's family out to Madinah himself.

He missed Badr, and the reason was obedience. Ten days before the army marched, the Prophet ﷺ had sent him and Sa'id ibn Zayd north to al-Hawra' to watch for the Quraysh caravan. They watched it pass and rode back with the report, not knowing the Muslims had already gone out. They reached Madinah on the day of the battle, rode after him, and met him returning at Turban. He gave them the shares and the reward of Badr, so that it was as though they had stood in the line.

After that he missed nothing — Uhud, the Ditch, every expedition. Once the Prophet ﷺ sent him out at the head of ten men and gave them their cry: 'Ya ushra' — O ten.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: The hand that caught an arrow for him
layers.content:
At Uhud the line broke and most of the army pulled away. Talhah stayed. He gave the Prophet ﷺ his allegiance to death and did not leave his side.

Malik ibn Zuhayr shot at the Prophet ﷺ. Talhah put his hand across the Prophet's ﷺ face and the arrow went into his little finger and left it half-dead. The pain pulled one sound out of him — 'Ah.' The Prophet ﷺ said that had he said 'In the Name of Allah' instead, he would have entered the Garden while the people watched. Years later Qays ibn Abi Hazim said he had seen the two paralysed fingers with which Talhah shielded the Prophet ﷺ that day.

His daughters Aisha and Umm Ishaq counted twenty-four wounds on their father from Uhud: his head laid open, his sciatic nerve severed, the finger dead, the rest scattered over his body. Other reports put the number of blows higher. He fainted; then he was the one carrying the Prophet ﷺ — front teeth broken, face torn — shaking under him, turning to fight off any idolater who came near, until he had him up in the ravine.

When Abu Bakr reached them the Prophet ﷺ said only: 'See to your companion.'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ on the arrow at Uhud: 'If he had said, In the Name of Allah, he would have entered the Garden while the people were looking' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: A man who could not sleep beside money
layers.content:
The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever wants to look at a man who has fulfilled his pledge, let him look at Talhah. The expression is the Qur'an's own — «فَمِنْهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ», among them is he who has fulfilled his vow.

He fulfilled it with his money as much as his body. He sold land to Uthman for seven hundred thousand dirhams. When the cash arrived he said: a man spends the night with this in his house not knowing what Allah has decreed for him. He kept messengers moving through Madinah until dawn and did not have a dirham left. His wife Su'da bint Awf once found him unsettled and asked why. Money, he said. Distribute it, she said. He distributed four hundred thousand.

He was killed at the Battle of the Camel in Jumada al-Akhira 36 AH, aged sixty-four. Muslims have differed since that day in how they read those events, and this app does not settle it. What the sources record is Ali receiving Talhah's son Imran, seating him on his own carpet, and saying he hoped he and Talhah would be among those Allah describes as brothers, on couches, facing one another (15:47).
layers.quran_ref: Quran 15:47 — «وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّن غِلٍّ إِخْوَانًا عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ» — 'And We shall strip away any rancour in their hearts — brothers, on couches, facing one another'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ: 'Whoever is happy to look at a man walking on the earth who has fulfilled his pledge should look at Talhah ibn Ubaydullah' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: Who walked Talhah to the Prophet ﷺ after he came back from Syria asking for news?

options.text: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam
Abu Bakr
His uncle from Banu Taym
The monk of Busra, who travelled with him

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Abu Bakr did not argue with him or debate the monk's report. He said: go to him and follow him, he is calling to the truth. Sometimes the most useful thing a believer can do is point.

quiz.prompt: Why was Talhah absent from the Battle of Badr?

options.text: He was still in Makkah, unable to emigrate
He was ill and the Prophet ﷺ excused him
The Prophet ﷺ had sent him north as a scout to watch for the Quraysh caravan
He was guarding the families in Madinah

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He and Sa'id ibn Zayd were doing exactly what they had been told to do, and it cost them the most celebrated day in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ gave them the shares and reward of Badr anyway. Obedience was counted, not attendance.

quiz.prompt: What happened to Talhah's hand at Uhud?

options.text: It was cut by a sword as he carried the banner
He shielded the Prophet's ﷺ face and an arrow left his finger paralysed
He broke it lifting the Prophet ﷺ into the ravine
It was burned pulling rings of mail from the Prophet's ﷺ cheek

quiz.citation: Reported from Amir ash-Sha'bi and from Qays ibn Abi Hazim — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Qays said he saw the two dead fingers himself, long afterwards. The wound never healed, and Talhah never seems to have wanted it to. Some scars are receipts.

quiz.prompt: Talhah sold land to Uthman for seven hundred thousand dirhams. What did he do with the money?

options.text: He bought more land at Qana with it
He gave it to the treasury in Madinah
He divided it between his sons
He sent messengers out through Madinah all night until none of it was left

quiz.citation: Reported from al-Hasan — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: His stated reason was not generosity but fear: a man sleeps a night with this in the house not knowing what Allah has decreed for him. He got rid of it the way you would get rid of something dangerous.

quiz.prompt: What did Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid do to Abu Bakr and Talhah when they became Muslim?

options.text: He drove them out of Makkah
He bound the two of them together with a single rope
He seized their trade goods
He had them beaten at the Ka'bah

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Their own clan, Banu Taym, did not intervene. The rope was meant as humiliation and became a title instead: the comrades, the two tied to one cord.

quiz.prompt: Talhah said the least fault a man can be charged with is sitting in his house. What keeps you sitting?

options.text: Not knowing which direction is the right one
Waiting until I am asked, so the responsibility is shared
Comfort — the house is warm and the road is not
I do move, but only on things nobody will judge me for

quiz.citation: Talhah's saying, reported from Qays — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said it as a merchant, about work, before he ever said it as a Muslim. Character formed in ordinary effort tends to hold when the stakes rise.

quiz.prompt: A stranger's warning — 'beware lest you be outstripped' — changed the direction of Talhah's life. When have you been given a warning like that?

options.text: I recognised it immediately and moved
I heard it, filed it, and came back to it much later
I argued with whoever said it
I am not sure I have ever been warned that directly

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of the monk of Busra — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The monk knew enough to describe the Prophet ﷺ and did not follow him. Talhah heard it secondhand and rode home. Information is not the same as response.

quiz.prompt: Talhah missed Badr because he was obeying an order elsewhere. How do you handle being absent from the moment everyone else remembers?

options.text: Badly — I want to be where the story is happening
I tell myself it is fine and quietly resent it
I have made peace with doing the part nobody will recount
It depends entirely on whether anyone notices my absence

quiz.citation: Reflection on Talhah's absence from Badr — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He rode back from al-Hawra' with news that was already old, having missed everything. The reward was assigned anyway. Allah is not audited by the crowd's memory.

quiz.prompt: Money made Talhah restless — he could not sleep with a large sum in the house. What does wealth do to you?
quiz.slider_label: What money does to your rest

options.text: It settles me. Having a cushion is peace
It makes me anxious about losing it
It makes me anxious about being asked for it
I have never had enough of it to find out

quiz.citation: Reported from al-Hasan and from Su'da bint Awf — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Notice that his wife's answer to his unease was 'distribute it,' not 'invest it.' She had understood what was actually bothering him.

quiz.prompt: Talhah died on the losing side of a fight between Muslims, and Ali still hoped to sit with him as a brother in the Garden. How do you hold people you believe were wrong?

options.text: If they were wrong, that is the whole story
I separate the error from the person, in theory at least
I leave the judgement alone entirely — it is not mine
I find it easier with the dead than with the living

quiz.citation: Ali receiving Imran ibn Talhah, citing Quran 15:47 — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ali quoted the verse about rancour being stripped from hearts, and whipped the man who objected to it. The generosity was not carelessness; it was a position he was willing to defend.
